- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 3–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, suppress upward momentum; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- Model often overreacts to recent price spikes — apply lagged mean reversion: if 3–5 day moving average is below forecast, reduce forecast by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to overfit recent volatility — use 10-day smoothed average as baseline for correction.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction of 1–3% per day until trend reverses.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is positive but price action shows early mean reversion, reduce forecast by 1–2% in first 5 days of horizon.
